title: Compact shadow-prefix overlay to dedupe near-duplicate prompts across requests
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We observe significant GPU memory duplication when users send prompts that are near-duplicates (small slot differences, punctuation, or variable user metadata). Current prefix dedupe heuristics require exact or near-exact fingerprints and fall back to entirely separate KV allocations for minor variations. This increases resident GPU memory and reduces effective cache hit rate for continuous batching workloads.

Proposal: Introduce a compact 'shadow-prefix overlay' mechanism: canonicalize and store a dense, canonical KV fragment for the most common prefix shapes and separately store tiny, delta-style overlays that capture small differences between the incoming prompt and the canonical fragment. At request time, the runtime composes the canonical KV with the overlay on the GPU via a lightweight byte-level patch/compose step scheduled onto the same CUDA stream as attention evaluation. Overlays are stored compressed in host-pinned memory and marshalled into ephemeral GPU overlay buffers only when a request uses them. For multi-request microbatches the runtime coalesces identical overlay patches and reuses composed KV views across requests in the same batch, enabling dedupe without duplicating full GPU slabs.

Key ideas: canonical fragment registry, lossy-but-safe normalization rules (whitespace, template slot tokenization), fingerprint-to-canonical mapping, overlay diff format (token index + replacement vector reference), ephemeral overlay apply kernel, batch-level overlay coalescing, eviction policies with overlay reference counts, metrics and fallbacks to full-copy if compose overhead exceeds threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce average GPU KV memory consumed per prefix by >= 18% for the targeted 95th-percentile workload in benchmark cluster A
End-to-end latency overhead for compose + apply < 1.5ms p50 for sequences <= 512 tokens in microbatch mode
Continuous batching throughput improves or remains neutral for mixed traffic with 15-30% near-duplicate rate

No correctness regressions: generated token outputs must be bitwise-equivalent to baseline when compose is used (tests for deterministic models), and within established quality thresholds for non-deterministic decoders
Rollout gating hooks present: runtime flag, per-tenant opt-in, and dashboard showing overlay hit/miss and compose cost
tasks: Design: finalize overlay delta format and canonicalization rules (owner: Ravi)
Prototype: host-side overlay serializer + small GPU compose kernel (owner: Eng-Intern)
Runtime: integrate compose step into the continuous-batching schedule and KV allocator (owner: Core Runtime)
Eviction: implement overlay-aware slab refcounts and compact eviction pass (owner: Memory Team)
Testing: create deterministic model tests and randomized prompt-fuzz harness for correctness
Benchmarking: run against benchmark cluster A workloads and collect memory/latency metrics
Docs & SDK: add flags and usage docs for Private/Dedicated customers
Rollout: staged rollout with feature flag, meta-level telemetry, and automatic rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Initial writeup and motivation. Sketched canonical registry idea after analyzing telemetry from Feb cluster runs.
2026-02-16 - Ravi Kapoor: Reviewed prototype constraints. Recommended compressing overlays with a simple LZ4 variant and pinning in host memory to avoid page faults during compose.

2026-02-20 - Sophia Liu (PM): Customer stories show many near-duplicate prompts with only slot differences; PM supports trying a conservative normalization first (strip repeated whitespace, canonicalize names).
2026-02-24 - Engineering review: Decided to target sequences <= 1024 tokens for v1 and to fall back to current dedupe on longer sequences. Agreed to instrument compose cost in microbench harness.
2026-02-27 - Memory team: Proposed an overlay reference-count table that cohabits with slab allocator metadata to avoid extra hashmaps on the hot path.

2026-03-01 - QA: Identified a race in continuous batching when multiple incoming requests point to the same canonical fragment but different overlay orderings; mitigation: canonicalize overlay application ordering and use atomic refcounts when pinning ephemeral composed views.

2026-03-02 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented initial host serializer and a CUDA compose kernel prototype. Early results: compose p50 ~1.2ms for 512-token candidate when overlays touch <6 token positions. Memory delta reduction ~22% in a synthetic near-duplicate tracer workload.
notes: Tradeoffs: Overlay approach reduces persistent GPU memory but adds ephemeral compose cost. For high-cardinality differences (many token changes) this degenerates to full-copy; runtime must detect and bypass overlays in that case.
Compatibility: Works with existing prefix registry if we add a canonical-tag mapping. For private deployments we will expose a toggle to disable lossy canonicalization rules.
Future: If successful, we can extend overlays to cross-model common prefixes (shared subgraph fragments) and to multimodal tokenization differences (image captioning templates).
